answer:
**Recommendation: cut to the note-writer, start charging, and get it into many more vet clinics. Don't switch to hospitals, and don't build a full practice-management system.**

You have one real signal. One clinic uses note-writing every day. The other 35+ features show no pull, and two of three pilots barely logged in. Building a complete system before charging would spend most of your roughly 9.5 months of runway without learning whether anyone will pay. Switching to hospitals would throw away your only signal for a market with slow, regulated buyers who take long procurement cycles to decide. Small vet clinics decide fast and judge on quality, which is where a two-person team wins.

**Next 8 weeks**

- **Week 1:** Hide everything except exam recording, clinical notes and possibly discharge instructions. Visit the daily-user clinic and learn exactly why it sticks. Ask the other two why they stopped. Ask the daily user to start paying, at roughly $300–500 per vet per month.
- **Weeks 2–3:** Fix whatever slows note-writing for the daily user. One founder does outreach full-time through calls, local vet networks and in-person visits. Book 40+ demos.
- **Weeks 4–8:** Run paid pilots with a 14-day trial and track weekly active vets. Aim for 10–15 paying clinics and steady week-over-week growth. Add features only when several paying clinics ask for the same thing.

**Assumptions:** The note quality is good enough to sign, and you can handle recording consent and data security.

**What would change this:**

- **Under five paying clinics after about 100 demos:** Revisit the price or the wedge.
- **High churn after the trial:** The notes aren't good enough, so fix quality before selling more.
- **Strong pull plus customers asking for billing or inventory:** Expand into adjacent features from that base.

Treat hospitals as a possible later market once you have revenue and proof.
